result.title: Separating Action Allocation from Image Matching in Visual Token Routing
result.summary: Adaptive visual token routers aim to save computation while preserving the image detail needed to answer each question. A higher average score could reflect better choices for individual images or more frequent use of high resolution on tasks that need it. We distinguish the two by keeping action counts fixed within each task and comparing the router's assignments with random pairings of the same actions and images. On equally weighted ChartQA and TextVQA, both Qwen2.5-VL-3B and -7B gain from matching but lose more from their action frequencies relative to a task table, with a 1.71-point gain and a 3.95-point loss on 7B. Exchanging the continuous resolutions chosen by the external selector CARES also lowers quality on 7B. When requests arrive with task labels, the table outscores the discrete router by 1.92 points and saves 31.76 ms per complete 7B request on average.

AI.brief_summary: 论文研究自适应视觉 token 路由，将路由收益分解为「动作分配」与「图像匹配」两部分，并通过固定任务内动作次数、与随机配对比较，在 ChartQA 和 TextVQA 上诊断 Qwen2.5-VL 路由器的实际收益来源。
AI.relevance_reason: 该诊断直接关联视觉证据筛选与「LOOK」的收益—成本问题：它区分了「更常启用高分辨率」与「为具体图像选对动作」两种贡献，可供核查视觉细节获取是否被有效使用，以及分辨率选择策略的评估是否混淆了任务难度与匹配质量。
